claims.statement: Thailand's visa exemption dropped from 60 to 30 days for most nationalities on 15 September 2026, with one further 30-day extension available.
The 30-day extension of the exemption costs 1,900 THB and is granted at the discretion of Thai Immigration, not automatically.
claims.limits: Amount not captured verbatim in this fetch of tatnews.org; corroborated by the site's own docs/dtv-fact-check.md and by dtv-visa-new-requirements-2026, already published.

claims.statement: Entries under the exemption through land border checkpoints are capped at two per calendar year, except for Malaysia, Brunei, Indonesia and Singapore.
Travellers admitted before 15 September 2026 keep the stay length they were granted on entry.
claims.limits: Not captured verbatim in this fetch of tatnews.org; corroborated by dtv-visa-new-requirements-2026, already published on this site.

claims.statement: The Thailand tourist visa (TR) gives 60 days, extendable once by 30 days for up to 90 days, and must be applied for before departure.

21 nationalities (Albania, Andorra, Colombia, Cuba, Dominica, Dominican Republic, Ecuador, Guatemala, Jamaica, Kosovo, Monaco, Morocco, Mexico, Panama, Papua New Guinea, San Marino, Sri Lanka, Tonga, Trinidad and Tobago, Uruguay, Uzbekistan) lose visa-free entry from 15 September 2026 and must apply for an e-Visa in advance.
claims.limits: Single-source claim, not independently corroborated at research time. Present as reported by visasnews.com, never as an unattributed absolute fact.

claims.statement: Proof of funds at arrival: 10,000 THB per person (20,000 THB family) under exemption/VOA/transit, 20,000 THB per person (40,000 THB family) under tourist/non-immigrant visas, under-12s exempt. Not a new rule: a 1980 Ministry of Interior requirement with amounts updated in 2000.
claims.limits: Source frames it as a 1980 rule with amounts updated in 2000; do not flatten to a bare '1980 amounts' claim.

claims.statement: Entry can be refused under Section 12(2) of the Immigration Act B.E. 2522 (1979) for insufficient means of subsistence.
claims.limits: The specifically requested source (library.siam-legal.com) returned HTTP 403 twice; this claim is corroborated via the hosted law text and independent secondary sources instead.

claims.statement: The TDAC (Thailand Digital Arrival Card) has been mandatory since 1 May 2025 for all foreign arrivals by air, land or sea, submitted up to 72 hours before arrival, via tdac.immigration.go.th.
claims.limits: Official government portal is a JavaScript SPA, not fetchable by automated tools; confirmed via a secondary source citing the Immigration Bureau and Bangkok Post.

claims.statement: Muay Thai remains a qualifying DTV soft-power activity; the 500,000 THB fund requirement, 10,000 THB fee and 5-year validity are unchanged by this reform.
claims.limits: Already verified project-side in docs/dtv-fact-check.md and published in dtv-visa-new-requirements-2026; not re-fetched externally for this article, carry over as-is without re-verification.
